I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the steadiest way for me to earn and reduce risk. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will manage that through harvest first, then I will plant summer maize right after. I will not spread my land across too many crops, because I want work that is familiar, input use I can control, and sales that are easy. I will use improved or hybrid seed, put most fertilizer into the wheat and maize because those are my main grain crops, irrigate several times since our area can be dry, and spray only as needed for the common field pests and diseases. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for the maize after wheat harvest because it is fast and practical for me, and I will keep the wheat under rotary-based field preparation as well. My goal is stable yield, manageable labor, and lower production risk rather than trying something fancy.
